fields.spec_version: Public webinar overview of MIPI SoundWire (21 January 2015); V09r04 entered 30-day final Voting Draft review at time of webinar; V1.0 ratification planned for mid-February 2015.
predecessor_protocols_replaced_or_unifie: I2S — two-pin or three-pin audio bus (BCK + WS + Data) without inherent multi-drop, command channel, or interrupt path. SoundWire offers lower pin count, clock scaling, dynamic slot mapping, burst mode, command embedded with data (no I2C/SPI needed), in-band interrupt capability (no GPIO), and PDM support — at cost of slight command overhead and inability to switch Master/Slave roles for clock.

PDM (Pulse Density Modulation) microphones — single-clock single-data stream with fixed oversampling. SoundWire adds clock scaling, embedded command/control, interrupt capability. PDM-mode overhead is ≈ 70% for dual-mic but less than 5% for single-mic; multi-lane SoundWire is lower power than equivalent PDM.
HDAudio — Intel's PC audio link. SoundWire offers clock scaling, lower pin count, PDM support, and scales to simple devices. Con: lower-bandwidth device-class functionality not yet standardized.

SLIMbus — earlier MIPI audio interface. SoundWire offers lower gate count for cost-sensitive devices, simpler protocol, low-latency PDM support, lower power with adjustable Frame size and DDR — at cost of no clock and manager hand-over capabilities (only Master and Monitor can send messages on SoundWire).
soundwire_release_history: June 2012 — Initial discussions in the MIPI LML Working Group.
Contributions from approximately 16 MIPI member companies (Intel and others).
V09r04 — Entered 30-day final Voting Draft review (around early 2015).
Mid-February 2015 — Planned V1.0 ratification by MIPI Alliance.
21 January 2015 — Public Overview Webinar (this PDF) presented by Pierre Bossart (Intel), MIPI LML WG Chair.
9 October 2014 — MIPI press release: 'MIPI Alliance Introduces MIPI SoundWire, a Comprehensive Audio Interface for Mobile and Mobile-Influenced Devices'.
scope_relative_to_other_mipi_specs: MIPI Alliance — Working Groups include Analog Control Interface, Battery Interface, Camera, Debug, Display High Speed Synchronous Interface, Low Latency Interface, Low Speed Multipoint Link (LML — owns SoundWire), Marketing, PHY (C/D/M), Reduced Input Output (RIO), RF Front-End, Sensor/I3C, Software, Technical Steering Group, Test, UniPro.

Within MIPI System Diagram: SoundWire is the interconnect between the Application Processor (Host) and Audio Codec / Microphones / Speakers; complementary to DSI (display), CSI (camera), I3C (sensors), UFS (storage), SLIMbus (legacy audio), GbT/SPP (debug), etc.

key_changes_vs_predecessors.summary: DDR 2-pin multi-drop bus with up to 11 Slaves vs point-to-point or shared 3-pin; embedded commands eliminate I2C/SPI sideband; in-band interrupt and wake; PDM support; dynamic bit allocation via Frame Shape; ClockStop for power. Slight command overhead; no Master/Slave role switching for clock.
Clock scaling, embedded command/control, interrupt capability. Multi-lane lower power than equivalent PDM. Overhead ≈ 70% for dual-mic and < 5% for single-mic mode.
Clock scaling, lower pin count, PDM, scales to simple devices. Con: lower-bandwidth device-class functionality not yet standardized.

Lower gate count for cost-sensitive devices, simpler protocol, low-latency PDM, lower power with adjustable frame size and DDR. Con: no clock and manager hand-over (only Master and Monitor can send messages).

backward_compat_traps.i2s: Three-pin (BCK + WS + Data) point-to-point or shared TDM, no command channel.
backward_compat_traps.soundwire: Two-pin DDR multi-drop with embedded commands + Modified-NRZI encoding + bus-keeper.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Devices designed for I2S cannot be dropped onto a SoundWire bus — the wire-level protocol is completely different. SoundWire is a SoC-level replacement, not a backward-compatibility layer.

backward_compat_traps.older_specs: Some audio interfaces pin precise jitter (ppm, ps) requirements.
backward_compat_traps.soundwire: No requirements on jitter (ppm, ps) in SoundWire spec — system-design concern only.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Implementers cannot rely on spec-mandated jitter — must allocate their own jitter budget for best audio quality, especially in multi-lane / multi-Slave configurations.

backward_compat_traps.mode1: Optional; context may be lost; re-enumeration required on wake.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Software wake-handler must check which mode the Slave was in before assuming Device Number, transport config, and interrupt masks are still valid; for Mode 1 the full enumeration + stream-setup must be repeated.

backward_compat_traps.normal_phy: Mandatory; meets default tDZ_Data_Max / tZD_Data_Min / tOH_Data_Min margins.
backward_compat_traps.high_phy: Beyond mandatory PHY timings; all components on the link must support the same requirements; mode identification via one bit of the static sync word; defined hand-over sequence.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Mixing a High-PHY-capable Slave with a Normal-PHY-only Slave on the same bus forces operation at Normal-PHY only.

fields.ipr_status_note: The MIPI SoundWire Specification is a MIPI Alliance specification; access to the full v1.0 spec is gated to MIPI members. The 2015 public overview webinar is the publicly-distributed summary used here as substitute documentation.
